findings.finding: Runner cleanup treated every nonzero Docker inspect as object absence, including daemon-unavailable and permission failures, so recovery could reach its first database read without proven quiescence. Inspect-then-create also left an orphan-client creation window.
findings.required_remediation: Accept absence only from an exact bounded Docker not-found result and fail closed on every other inspect failure. Create and identity-seal both fixed production runners before durable production intent; recovery may only quiesce and restart those already sealed containers.

findings.finding: Interrupted database recovery trusted the stored backup hash and flags without proving the root-owned backup still existed with the recorded mode, size and current hash before repair or retry.
findings.required_remediation: Before the first recovery database read or mutation, re-open the exact backup through the secure-file boundary and prove ownership, mode, link count, bounded exact byte count and a freshly computed exact SHA256.
